essence: Twenty-nine approximations that cancel themselves: no helper, no hinderer (1); sourced yet self-born (2); how could things reach His path (3); the sated wander (4); timeless vision (5); entering by resolve (6); pure play (7); fearless dwelling (8); dissolved, drunk, wandering (9); pretense suffices (10); one-taste drinking (11); the essence-extract (12); inside/outside puzzle (13); facing everywhere in agitation (14); reveal the abode (15); fled yet never unseen (16); flood to joy (17); grain for worship-exchange (18); seeing each thing, seeing You (19); unhaunting mind questioned (20); ploughmen see (21); feast unstopped (22); insight, power, unpausing worship (23); sense-heap as His limb (24); roaming mind, skilled service (25); slave by His will, yet faceless (26); opponents wondered at (27); things as things by His being (28); nothing/something grammar of worship (29).

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as pointing to the secret
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of pointing (nirdeśa); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at approximations that cancel themselves. The rasa is the tranquility of pointing — no exposition, only indication; each verse a finger, none the moon. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as śānta: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute pointed to, never stated.
